sourceInformation.source: Attack of the Timelord! (1982), Odyssey², Ed Averett / North American Philips
sourceInformation.perspective: Fixed overhead screen aligned shooting plane; horizontal defense lane
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 0.89.1 at 8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691 (three focused patches); JavaScript, native Canvas 2D and Web Audio; AI Hub protocol 1 / session client 1.4.0 at 35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869; pinned PeerJS 1.5.5; esbuild 0.27.0 for single-file assembly.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original native procedural pixel art with shaded machines, geometric weapons, layered rainbow rift and expressive projected tyrant
sourceInformation.animation: Native E.Path Catmull formations, E.sprite / E.anim, procedural banking, recoil, facial expressions and geometric impact particles
sourceInformation.audio: Original code synthesized score, effects and Animalese style nonsense voice; independent music/effects/voice buses; music defaults to 10%; no audio files or TTS
sourceInformation.online: One-to-four-player host-authoritative shared campaign through AI Hub and standalone public PeerJS/WebRTC rooms. Real two-context data links, ready/start, actions, damage, brake, result, replay and disconnect tested. Independent monotonic host clock does not require rendering. Public signaling can time out; restrictive NATs may require TURN. Universal internet reachability is unknown.
sourceInformation.testing: One quiet command covers pure state and legitimate solo/four-player campaigns, native engine drawing/clock/pause/persistence, final HTML file input and storage in Chromium/WebKit/Firefox, real stub-controller and emulated touch, offline audio signals, all four official Hub scenarios, and actual public WebRTC. No performance gates. Physical controllers, real phones, TV viewing and subjective listening were unavailable.
sourceInformation.research: North American instruction manual, William Cassidy hands-on review, gameplay image and box art inspected; no gameplay video viewed; original precise steering, timings and continuous musical score unknown

testingFeedback: Automated and visual checks caught 10 distinct game defects; focused integration review found 16 more. All 26 were fixed. Test setup mistakes are excluded. The full check results and finding ledger are in docs/verification.md and test-artifacts/verification.json.

Five of the 26 findings could block a core flow: renderer context, canvas sizing, narrow-screen cropping, guest results, and a backgrounded authoritative host. Four were caught by testing and one by review.

The actual packaged two-context WebRTC test exposed dependence on background animation frames; the fix gave networking an independent fixed-step clock. Legitimate complete campaign tests also prevented softlocks.
A boot-only check: the engine catches draw exceptions internally, so a loaded document alone did not establish that the arena rendered or the game played.
engineFeedback: The complete dependency-free procedural renderer, paths, code audio, device input, shell and settings made an inspectable single-file game practical.
The native renderer context is r.ctx, not r.g; Arcade turns are alternating, not simultaneous. Both were resolved against source and tests.
A deterministic shared simulation, authoritative networking protocol, standalone room flow and independent network clock.
Separating canonical simulation and input freshness from rendering, local shell pause and background tab timing.

Patched only the bundled full engine: session-only persist:false settings, fixed-resolution fractional downscaling with stable margins, and same-screen Shell focus preservation for controller pickers.
Provide a first-class independent authoritative clock and a documented shared-world adapter seam.
promptFeedback: The source references, exact weapon behavior and explicit verification contracts made the intended game concrete.
TASK.md calls it a feature-complete demo while PLAN.md specifies a whole campaign; I followed PLAN.md and built all eight waves plus the finale.
Making the actual single-file game agree across solo, headless Hub hosting, real WebRTC rooms and all input devices, including teardown and replay.
Ship versioned Hub harness support with the engine handoff so implementation and protocol checks share one pinned target.

aiHub.name: Attack of the Timelout
aiHub.tagline: Shoot his fleet. Steal his seconds.
aiHub.description: A petty temporal tyrant sends curling fleets and four kinds of interceptable weapons. Defend the bottom rail, charge a time brake, and close the rift across eight waves and a three-phase finale, solo or with up to four pilots.
aiHub.controls: Left stick / D-pad or A/D / arrows to slide; Cross / R2 or Space / left mouse to fire; Square / L2 or Shift / right mouse to brake; Options / Escape for menu.
